svg.title: Step 4 polish 03: the sound desk sub-pages Library, Limits and categories, Log
svg.text: 03 · The sound desk: Library, Limits and categories, Log (desktop, 1280 px, drawn at 62 %)
The other three sub-pages under the same master strip. Book shots O9 (library, budget, categories, log), O11, O12.
Library
Limits and categories
Log

g.text: Or drop MP3 or OGG files here.
At most 30 s and 1 MiB each; a warning over 10 s. The default pack is CC0, with a credits file.
Urgent always passes and still counts. One sound at a time per zone.
Seconds between sounds of one source
Six, fixed, in this order: a higher one waits for none below it. Events add cues, never categories.
The zone has no sound screen
Silent at calm: the zone is at calm

svg.text: What changed and why
Upload as one wide target
A button and a drop area with the rules in words, instead of the browser’s file input (O9).
Sounds as cards with themed players
Each sound is a card: play and stop, waveform, length, licence and the cues that use it by name.
O9 had a table of the browser’s light-grey players.
One playing at a time
Starting one stops the other; the playing card is outlined.
The budget with sliders and meters
Sounds an hour and a minute are sliders; the per-source gap is a stepper. The zone table shows
its use as meters and says in words what is missing and where to fix it ("None · Set one in
Devices"), where O9 and O12 said only "no sound screen".
Categories as rows of controls
Level as a slider; interrupts and calm as two-way switches; the fixed order stated in words
above them. O9 had number boxes and checkboxes.
No typed numbers
Every level and limit on the desk is a slider or a stepper.
The log filters
Search, outcome chips and a zone switch; newest first.
Reasons in words
Each row says what happened in a sentence ("Not again for 2 min: played 21:29:10"); the reason
code is the grey second line. O9 led with the code.
